title: The 3 Best Patio Heaters for Covered Porches
h1: The 3 Best Patio Heaters for Covered Porches
metaDescription: Our 3 picks for patio heaters for covered porches, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at patio heaters for covered porches using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Solaira Cosy Infrared Heater
products.blurb: Key specs: 1500W / 120V quartz infrared element, 10 by 10 foot coverage area, Ceiling or wall mount, 4-inch slim housing.
strengths: Ceiling mount uses zero floor space, ideal for a furnished covered porch
No combustion byproducts, so it's genuinely safer in a lower-airflow covered space
Near-instant quartz warmup means no waiting for the space to feel the effect
limitations: Requires a dedicated circuit for permanent installation
Higher price than any propane option on this list
Coverage is fixed to roughly a 10 by 10 foot zone directly below and in front of it
features: Ceiling or wall mount, 4-inch slim housing
No combustion, no carbon monoxide risk

products.name: Dr. Infrared Heater Carbon Infrared Patio Heater
products.blurb: Key specs: 120V / 1500W carbon infrared element, 3 heat settings, IP55 weatherproof rating.
strengths: IP55 rating handles the humidity and occasional wind-blown rain a covered porch still gets
Multiple mount options let you go ceiling, wall, or freestanding depending on the porch layout
limitations: Slightly smaller effective coverage area than the Solaira at the same wattage
Included tripod is a lower-end accessory compared to a permanent mount
Needs an outdoor-rated outlet or hardwire within reach
features: Wall, ceiling, or freestanding with included tripod

products.name: Fire Sense 60262 Tabletop Patio Heater
products.blurb: Key specs: 10,000 BTU propane burner, Stainless steel tabletop design, Auto-shutoff tilt valve.
strengths: Lower flame height than a full-size standing heater, easier to keep within overhead clearance limits
Auto-shutoff tilt valve adds a margin of safety under a roof
Inexpensive way to add heat to a covered porch that already has good airflow on two sides
limitations: Still an open flame, unsuitable for a fully enclosed or low-airflow porch regardless of height
Requires verifying overhead clearance against the manufacturer's spec before using indoors-adjacent
Smaller heat radius than the electric mounted options

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
